claims.text: Controlled additive manufacturing or directional solidification can produce an oriented lamellar or columnar microstructure in tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers.
The oriented lamellae or columnar grains should be aligned normal to the imposed heat flux.
Conventional non-oriented tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers have high mechanical robustness.
Irregular boundaries in conventional non-oriented tungsten-based HEAs limit heat-transfer capability.
Plasma-facing reactor components operate under high-temperature and high-heat-flux conditions.
The proposed improvement should hold at approximately 800–1000 °C under concurrent high thermal flux and mechanical loading.
Aligned lamellae or columnar grains provide continuous, low-impedance thermal pathways.
The oriented microstructure sustains a robust multiphase network that supports mechanical loads.
Microstructural alignment minimizes thermal-boundary scattering along the heat-transfer direction.
Reduced thermal-boundary scattering increases effective thermal conductivity.
Directionally solidified columnar microstructures can preserve or improve HEA mechanical strength relative to ordinary casting.
A directionally solidified tungsten-based HEA will have higher thermal conductivity than a conventional isotropic tungsten-based HEA.
The directionally solidified tungsten-based HEA will maintain comparable high-temperature strength.
The directionally solidified tungsten-based HEA will maintain comparable creep resistance.
Loss of microstructural alignment during manufacturing may negate the thermal benefit.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity enhancement is not yet quantified.
The effects of aging and irradiation on the proposed enhancement remain unquantified.
